  "markdown_report": "Select a **mutation-calibrated temporal diagnostic** before changing NextItNet training. At 10% progress, establishing which probes detect implementation defects is a feasible foundation; current evidence does not establish a temporal modeling failure.

Three starting insights guide this choice. First, uniform training-audit HR@10 reaches 0.9362–0.9953, while competitive candidates reduce it. This supports candidate sensitivity, but fitted targets cannot establish generalization. Second, Movies_and_TV loses 0.2652 HR@10 with prefix-lexical competitors. That motivates measuring precise discrimination without inferring incompatibility or satisfied needs. Third, deployment parity and internal category identity are unavailable. These gaps limit conclusions even when in-memory checks pass.

Three literature insights refine the approach. NextItNet’s causal convolutions imply future-invariance and receptive-field constraints [1]. These provide implementation checks independent of accuracy. History-shuffling research finds heterogeneous sequential structure [2]. Consequently, shuffle sensitivity alone cannot establish useful temporal reasoning. Conditional permutation methods depend on the replacement distribution [3]. Matching can improve descriptive controls, but does not automatically justify causal claims or calibrated p-values.

The resulting framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation integrity | Causality, topology, readout checks | Probe detection reliability |
| Temporal dependence | Distance-resolved matched swaps | Useful versus implausible sensitivity |
| Candidate discrimination | Frozen competitive candidates | Transfer to pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Mutation-calibrated probes [1] | 4/7/3 | Originality: useful integration, established testing principle. Potential: makes diagnosis actionable, cannot guarantee accuracy. Difficulty: no retraining, functional mutants need care. |
| Matched local history swaps [2,3] | 6/7/6 | Originality: controlled adaptation, matching is established. Potential: isolates distance effects, residual mismatch persists. Difficulty: reuses scoring, sparse support complicates matching. |
| Fixed uniform/frequency negative mixture [4] | 2/6/3 | Originality: direct application, already proposed upstream. Potential: targets observed competition, false negatives may harm validation. Difficulty: small sampler change, exact pool handling matters. |

For the selected idea, compare each clean diagnostic with isolated count-minus-one readout, centered-padding causality, and altered-dilation mutants. Use disposable functional execution of the same fitted weights; never train, select, save, or deploy a mutant. Derive expected receptive fields independently from the clean convolution configuration. Report defect-specific detection, clean alarms, support and numerical tolerances. Weak response within a reachable field is not a defect.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, its interpreter, ModelView interfaces, final-nonpadding readout, and one NextItNet checkpoint per category. Bound diagnostics to four batches and 32 rows per batch; restore modes, hooks and RNG states. Keep all four routes, seeds, training limits and evaluator unchanged. Report reload parity as unavailable without a host interface. These diagnostics support debugging; only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects accuracy improvements.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Calibrate the existing NextItNet structural and distance-resolved probes against isolated, deliberately injected inference defects. Compare clean execution with readout, causality and dilation mutants using the same fitted parameters and bounded training examples. Mutants are disposable diagnostic executions, never additional fitted predictors or deployment candidates.",
    "motivation": "The supplied measurements establish competitive-candidate sensitivity but do not establish defective temporal reasoning. Low sampled-pair error and modest positive embedding cosine do not demonstrate correct deployment. Probe calibration can distinguish detectable implementation faults from ordinary weak learned sensitivity before spending the shared GPU budget on another training intervention.",
    "implementation_notes": "Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing measured diagnostics and explicit unavailable statuses. Use view.model as the actual clean trained module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Never require unavailable review or item attributes.

Snapshot at most four batches and 32 rows per batch using the existing family-specific loader. Select finite nonpadding positions; final readout uses the largest nonzero index, excluding all-padding rows. Record comparison support and sequence lengths. Loader rows lack stable user identities, so report descriptive row-level results without user-bootstrap intervals.

Before examining results, specify separate mutant implementations: count-minus-one readout; centered convolution padding that exposes future tokens while preserving output shape; and one altered convolution dilation with correspondingly adjusted causal padding. Derive the reference offset set from every conv1/conv2 kernel and dilation in the clean residual stack, including identity branches. Verify each mutant was activated and record affected layers and eligible examples. Do not treat an unchanged feature inside the theoretical receptive field as failure. Dilation mutants may escape behavioral detection when learned weights are insensitive; record that limitation.

Use temporary functional wrappers or carefully scoped hooks rather than saved alternative checkpoints. For future-invariance, modify future tokens and compare earlier features. For topology checks, perturb occupied positions outside the clean reachable-offset set. For readout checks, compare the selected feature index with the largest nonpadding index; include short left-padded rows on which count-minus-one differs. Predeclare float32 tolerances, for example rtol=1e-4 and atol=1e-5, and report actual errors alongside threshold decisions. Structural configuration mismatch and behavioral detection must be separate outputs.

Run in eval/no_grad mode. Restore every module's training flag, RNG states and temporary hooks in finally; confirm the clean state dictionary is unchanged. Report clean violation counts, per-mutant eligible rows, detection counts, observed maximum errors and exclusions. Describe clean-model alarms as observed violations until the clean implementation has been independently verified. No generic mutation-detection percentage should be imported from another architecture.

Explicit category routing should be supplied through the existing host context when available. Never infer category from catalog size or silently declare index 0 correct. Return unknown identity and unavailable category-macro results otherwise. Deployment reload parity remains unavailable without a host execution interface.

No training or predictor change is required for this diagnostic proposal. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain trial-local. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Execute on one GPU within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Deploy exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, without score fusion or checkpoint averaging.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = capture_modes_rng_and_clean_state_digest(self.view.model)
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                batches = snapshot_batches(train_loader, max_batches=4, max_rows=32)
                reference = derive_clean_residual_convolution_offsets(self.view.model)
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_probes(batches)
                clean = run_invariants(
                    self.view, batches, reference,
                    readout='largest_nonzero_index',
                    rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
                results = {}
                for defect in ['count_minus_one', 'future_exposing_padding',
                               'single_layer_dilation_change']:
                    with disposable_functional_mutant(self.view.model, defect) as mutant:
                        results[defect] = run_fault_specific_checks(
                            mutant, batches, clean_reference=reference,
                            report_structural_and_behavioral_detection_separately=True)
                return {
                    'metrics': merge(metrics, clean, results,
                                     support_exclusions_and_unavailable_interfaces()),
                    'metric_definitions': merge(definitions, calibration_definitions())
                }
        finally:
            remove_temporary_hooks()
            restore_modes_and_rng(saved)
            assert_clean_state_digest_unchanged(saved)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt(
        measured_metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        instructions=['Separate implementation violations from learned sensitivity.',
                      'Report eligibility, exclusions and mutant activation.',
                      'Do not infer validation accuracy, intent or compatibility.',
                      'Retain unavailable deployment checks as unavailable.'])",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "Combines NextItNet receptive-field analysis, left-padding readout checks and controlled inference mutations into a family-specific diagnostic calibration.",
      "negative": "Mutation testing and architectural invariants are established; the contribution is their careful integration rather than a new recommendation algorithm."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 7,
      "positive": "Provides a reusable basis for interpreting later temporal interventions and detecting predictor regressions without fitting additional recommendation models.",
      "negative": "Passing the suite cannot establish deployment parity, useful temporal reasoning or improved validation HR@10; its coverage is limited to specified defects and supported examples."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 3,
      "positive": "Reuses the supplied probes, actual convolution stack and bounded batches without retraining or metadata indexing.",
      "negative": "Functional padding and dilation mutants must preserve tensor shapes and clean state; an independently derived reference is necessary to avoid circular checks."
    }
  },
  "related_work": [
    {
      "title": "[1] NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation",
      "link": "https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf",
      "contributions": [
        "Provides the causal dilated residual convolution architecture underlying the required model family.",
        "Supplies architectural grounds for future-invariance and receptive-field checks."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish the proposed mutation-calibration protocol or its detection coverage.",
        "Architectural reachability does not imply a nonzero learned behavioral effect."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[2] Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008",
      "contributions": [
        "Studies original and shuffled histories across multiple datasets.",
        "Motivates testing whether measured order sensitivity corresponds to useful sequential information."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Unrestricted shuffling can alter history plausibility.",
        "Its findings do not establish a temporal failure in the supplied fitted NextItNet models."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[3] The Conditional Permutation Test for Independence While Controlling for Confounders",
      "link": "https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/article/82/1/175/7056014",
      "contributions": [
        "Develops conditional permutation methodology that preserves dependence on observed confounders.",
        "Motivates controlled replacements rather than arbitrary history corruption."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Formal calibration depends on conditional-distribution assumptions.",
        "The suggested matched-history recommendation diagnostic is an adaptation, not an established application from this paper."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[4] Supplied training-candidate stress audit and prior research proposal",
      "link": "",
      "contributions": [
        "Reports weaker fitted-target ranking against frequency-weighted and lexical competitors across the four categories.",
        "Proposes a fixed uniform/frequency training-negative mixture as a minimal future intervention."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Training-audit metrics are not pinned validation metrics.",
        "Category identity and generated-predictor reload parity remain unavailable; competitor items are not verified negatives."
      ]
    }
  ]
